subject: Clarify: where LLM requests transit, are stored, and deletion commitments
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@cardinalhealth.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cardinal Health Security <sec-team@cardinalhealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where data actually "touches" and what you delete

Connor —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A quick, practical security question from our InfoSec team: can you confirm exactly where (regions and subprocessors) Cardinal requests are processed, whether any request or derived artifacts are stored at rest outside the US, and what your deletion commitments are for request content and transient logs? They asked for a simple mapping we can include in our intake.

High level answers are fine but they also asked for the list of subprocessors involved in each hop (e.g., CDN, object store, analytics) and the default retention windows for request content, KV caches, and operational logs.

Can you point me to a diagram or summary we can share? If it's better to hop on a short call with one of your compliance folks, happy to schedule.

Best,
Sophie Lang
Director, Product Integrations
Cardinal Health AI

--
Cardinal Health AI — sophie.lang@cardinalhealth.ai

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where data actually "touches" and what you delete

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the clear ask. I can summarize the high-level flow here and loop in Marissa (compliance) for a detailed subprocessors list and the official retention commitments. High-level answers below; Marissa will attach a diagram and inventory.

High-level summary (short):
- In the default hosted plan, inference requests from Cardinal users enter our US frontends (primary: us-west-2).
- Requests are routed to the nearest available execution pool (typically us-west-2 or us-east-1) for low latency; we support explicit region pins for Dedicated/Private customers.
- We use short-lived KV caches and ephemeral GPU-resident state; persistent storage is only used when customers store embeddings, uploads, or enable logs/analytics.

Questions for InfoSec so the inventory is precise:
1) Do you need evidence of where intermediate caching or CDN edges may see requests (e.g., FastEdge CDN) or is a backend-only map sufficient?
2) Do you have a maximum retention box (e.g., all request content must be deleted within 30 days) we should validate against?

If it helps, Marissa can attach (A) a processing-location PDF, (B) a subprocessor inventory spreadsheet, and (C) our standard retention table. Want me to bring that into this thread?

Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@cardinalhealth.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where data actually "touches" and what you delete

On Thu, Mar 22, 2028 at 9:20 AM Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sophie —
> 
> Thanks for the clear ask. I can summarize the high-level flow here and loop in Marissa (compliance) for a detailed subprocessors list and the official retention commitments. High-level answers below; Marissa will attach a diagram and inventory.

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear framing. Attaching the requested artifacts: residency-diagram.pdf (visual map), subprocessor-inventory.xlsx (detailed vendor list by hop) and redwood-dataflow-notes.txt (compact retention table + controls). I pasted the most important bits inline so you can copy into your intake doc.

1) Regions and where requests execute (hosted default)
- Ingress/front door: our API edge runs in us-west-2 (primary) with failover to us-east-1. CDN edges (FastEdge) may cache public docs/large assets; they do not persist request payloads.
- Execution: inference executes on GPU pools in us-west-2 or us-east-1 by default. For EU customers we also have eu-west-1 pools; APAC pools are available in ap-southeast-1 on request.
- Storage: persistent storage (S3 buckets) used only for: user-uploaded artifacts, saved embeddings, and long-term logs (when enabled). Default hosted does not persist request payloads to S3 unless logging is explicitly turned on.

2) Subprocessors by hop (summary)
- Front door / edge: FastEdge CDN (edge caching), CloudRouter (managed DNS / routing)
- Execution / compute: AWS EC2/GPU (us-west-2 / us-east-1 / eu-west-1), CUDA runtime delivered by our serving runtime layer
- Short-term caching: MemKv (managed by CacheCorp) — in-memory, TTL-based
- Object storage (optional persistent artifacts): AWS S3 (regional buckets per account)
- Observability/analytics (opt-in): MetricsHub, LogStore (logs are routed to a customer-segregated bucket if enabled)
- Platform operations: Pagerline (on-call routing), AuditTrail (compliance logs stored in encrypted vault)

3) Cross-border transfer notes
- For hosted customers on default settings, request metadata and non-persistent execution state are processed within US regions; we do not proactively transfer request payloads to other continents without a region pin or customer request.
- When we autoscale or failover for availability, requests may be routed to a different US region (us-west-2 <-> us-east-1). For customers with explicit EU residency requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments; we offer EU-only execution pools and regional S3 buckets.

4) Retention commitments (defaults; we can create a shorter SLA on contract)
- Request payloads (unless logging enabled): not written to persistent object storage by default — ephemeral GPU/host memory only; effective retention: ephemeral only (seconds to minutes), except for cached prefixes in MemKv (default TTL 300s).
- KV cache / prefix caches: default TTL 300 seconds (5 minutes); can be pinned shorter in config.
- Saved embeddings & customer-saved artifacts: persisted until customer deletes or applies their retention policy; by default stored in the account's regional S3 bucket.
- Operational logs (if enabled by customer): default retention 90 days, archived for 1 year for customers on enterprise plan only.
- Audit logs (security): retained for 1 year by default, exportable on request.

5) Deletion workflows and guarantees
- Ephemeral state: cleared automatically after execution; no action required.
- Persistent artifacts & embeddings: deleted within 24 hours of user-initiated deletion; we provide asynchronous erasure confirmation (audit token) when erasure completes.
- Logs & observability: when customer requests deletion of logs, we purge from active indices within 48 hours; archived copies removed per the retention schedule and any legal hold requests considered.

6) Evidence we can provide (on request)
- Processing-location diagram (attached)
- Subprocessor inventory with regional mappings (attached)
- Sample erasure confirmation token/process flow (we can run a test erasure)
- SOC2 controls mapping for hosted ingestion and deletion workflows

Notes / caveats
- If you require absolute never-leave-US guarantees for any transient diagnostic traces from our platform, we'll recommend either (A) Dedicated capacity with EU/US-only execution pools or (B) Private deployment where the control plane is also inside your VPC.
- If Cardinal plans to enable detailed request logging or store embeddings, we will provision regional S3 buckets and document exact bucket ARNs for your procurement team.

If you want, I can join a 30-minute call with your InfoSec to walk the diagram and answer any procurement-level questions. Connor — happy for you to book time with Sophie?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Compliance & Customer Trust
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199
